value prop:   when a prospect replies to a campaign, the agent you configured for that campaign handles it — not a generic support bot blind to the outbound context — and you choose auto-send or draft-for-review (auto-send is opt-in, off by default). the campaign and the inbox are the same runtime, from $25/mo, so a reply never falls between the two tools.

proof points: VERIFIED shipped (g8 `ai_inbox` reconciliation 2026-07-06): the reply agent is selected per campaign via a `campaign_agent_id` 4-tier fallback (`ai_inbox/agents/core/workflow.py`) — the campaign's configured agent (its own persona/instructions) answers · auto-send is gated by `auto_respond` (defaults OFF; auto-sends only when the channel is RUNNING, otherwise routes to a draft) — configurable draft-vs-send · AI draft + route across email, chat, SMS, LinkedIn, meetings into one timeline (`workflow.py`, `services/universal_activity.py`) · from $25/mo, free PAYG (brief 2026-06-26).
              ⚠ NOT shipped today (do NOT claim in copy): the reply draft does NOT dynamically thread the live campaign/sequence content into the LLM prompt — the campaign-specificity comes from WHICH agent answers (its configured persona/instructions), not from per-reply injection of the sequence text. Say "the campaign's agent handles the reply," never "it reads your sequence and replies in its context." · any reply-rate / time-to-reply lift stat: NEEDS-VERIFICATION.

CTA (one):    the free PAYG onramp — run one campaign and let its agent handle the replies (draft mode first)

sequence outline (3 touches max):
  1. their world first — you send outbound, and when someone replies it drops into a support inbox that has no idea they're a prospect mid-campaign. so the reply gets a canned ticket answer or waits behind a refund request.
  2. the cost of the seam — that's your warmest replies handled by the coldest process, because your outbound tool and your inbox are separate islands. no helpdesk can fix it — it was never connected to the campaign.
  3. the walk-away — graph8 runs the campaign and the inbox on one runtime, so the agent you set up for that campaign handles its replies, and you pick auto-send or draft. start free on PAYG in draft mode and watch it. reply and I'll send the link.

email approach: matter_of_fact (MOF) — the "warm replies, cold process" observation carries itself. one_question_hyper (1Q) variant ("when a prospect replies to your sequence, does your inbox know they're a prospect?"). See `reference/email-prompts/`.

overlap note: targets the helpdesk∩outbound intersection — collides with `sequencer` (the outbound side) and `crm` at the data layer; ai-inbox wins where the pain is framed as the inbound-reply experience. Draws on the shared support-tool TAM — separate wave from the other ai-inbox cells (wave discipline in program-design.md).

priority:     Tier-1 — the program's sharpest VERIFIED differentiator: only a vendor running outbound and the inbox on one runtime can make this claim, and both halves (per-campaign agent + auto-send mode) ship today. Replaces the withdrawn value-routing flagship.
